title: Four-additive spanners with four-thirds-power size
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C>0\) such that every connected simple undirected unweighted graph \(G\) on \(n\ge2\) vertices has a spanning subgraph \(H\) with \[|E(H)|\le Cn^{4/3}\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_H(u,v)\le d_G(u,v)+4\quad\text{for all }u,v\in V(G)?\] Distances count edges. New edges, weights and vertices are not permitted, and no construction-time bound is imposed.
context:
The survey asks whether +4 error can be achieved with \(O(n^{4/3})\) edges, compared with the known exponent \(7/5\). This is a major gap in the sparsity of additive distance-preserving subgraphs.

The 2025 deterministic construction improves construction time while retaining the soft-\(O(n^{7/5})\) edge bound. The source does not supply an \(n^{4/3}\) upper bound.

Six-additive spanners achieve the \(4/3\) exponent, and general lower bounds obstruct beating that exponent for constant additive error. The +4 regime therefore asks whether a basic sparsity threshold can be reached with a smaller distance error.

The selected question is the survey’s \(O(n^{4/3})\) upper-bound target. The constant is universal and no growing logarithmic factor is hidden. A refutation need not determine the alternative optimal edge count.

The question of how additive error must grow when only \(O(n)\) edges are allowed is separately retained as TCS-6785. This card keeps the important +4 regime, rather than bundling weighted, variable-error and failure-tolerant models.
why: The +4 additive-spanner regime is the classical remaining constant-error sparsity-exponent gap, making it a central distance-compression problem rather than a peripheral parameter choice.
status_note: The +4 sparsity gap remains in the 2025 primary source. The broader variable-error linear-size question is retained separately as TCS-6785.

sentences: A spanner retains a subset of graph edges while approximately preserving distances.
This card permits an additive increase of at most four edges for every vertex pair.
It asks whether the retained subgraph always needs only a constant times n to the four-thirds edges.
Only original unweighted edges may be retained.
The statement is an existence question independent of construction time.

definitions: Each original edge has length one. \(d_{G}(u,v)\) is the minimum number of edges in a path, with \(d_{G}(u,u)=0\). A spanning subgraph H has the same vertex set and a subset of G’s edges, with unchanged unit lengths. If u,v are disconnected in H put \(d_{H}(u,v)=\infty\), so the requirement forces H to be connected. The lower inequality \(d_{H}(u,v)\ge d_{G}(u,v)\) follows from being a subgraph. The cost is number of retained edges; neither construction time nor weights, shortcuts, missing vertices, terminal subsets or faults are part of the model. New weighted edges would be an emulator and are not allowed. Restricting to connected inputs only removes disconnected bookkeeping; applying a universal bound componentwise recovers its usual all-graph form.
answer_criterion: Give a complete, mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed assertion or of its logical negation, with exactly the stated model, quantifier order and parameter dependence. A bound for a restricted subclass or one particular algorithm is insufficient to refute a universal existence assertion. Determining the entire optimal rate or a numerical approximation to it is not required.
